chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Umayra, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'a, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: 'Is everything in the Book of God and the sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), or do you [the Imams] pronounce upon it [independently]?'
He said: 'Rather, everything is in the Book of God and the sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.بَلْ: Rather/Nay — Arabic corrective-confirmatory particle (iḍrāb), here strongly affirming the questioner's implied premise
key_terms.تَقُولُونَ: You [plural] say/pronounce — implying independent juristic opinion (ra'y); the Imam's answer rejects this notion
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ: Sunnah of His Prophet — prophetic tradition comprising words, actions, and tacit approvals
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: Book of God — the Quran, primary revealed source of Islamic law and guidance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) say when asked whether everything is contained in the Book of God and the sunnah of the Prophet, or whether the Imams add their own rulings?
ai.summary: Sama'a ibn Mihran asked Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) whether all religious matters are encompassed entirely within the Quran and the Prophet's sunnah, or whether the Imams contribute rulings of their own independent authority. The Imam answered emphatically with the corrective particle 'bal' (rather/nay), affirming that everything is indeed in the Book of God and the sunnah of His Prophet — a creedal statement asserting that the Imams' teachings derive from and extend these two sources, not supplement them with independent opinion (ra'y).
